name: Farrah Chaichi
occupation: State Representative; intake specialist at Stoel Rives (per Capital Chronicle)

bio.statement: The Oregon Capital Chronicle's 2026 voter guide describes Chaichi as an intake specialist at Stoel Rives who has served in the Oregon House since 2023.
bio.excerpt: Farrah Chaichi, an intake specialist at Stoel Rives, has served in the Oregon House since 2023.

source.publisher: Oregon Capital Chronicle 2026 voter guide (Democratic primary, House District 35)

bio.statement: In her Oregon Legislature biography, Chaichi says she studied criminal justice and political science at Seattle University.
bio.excerpt: I went to Seattle University where I studied Criminal Justice and Political Science

bio.statement: In her voters' pamphlet statement, Chaichi lists her occupation as state representative, with a background in intake and conflicts at Stoel Rives and compliance at Daimler Truck.
bio.excerpt: Occupation: State Representative Occupational Background: Intake and Conflicts - Stoel Rives; Compliance, Daimler Truck

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 54

bio.statement: Chaichi lists a master's from George Washington University and a B.A. from Seattle University.
bio.excerpt: Educational Background: Master of Professional Studies, George Washington University; B.A., Seattle University; Beaverton HS

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 54

bio.statement: Chaichi lists the Beaverton Human Rights Advisory Commission.
bio.excerpt: Prior Governmental Experience: Beaverton Human Rights Advisory Commission

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 54

positions.statement: In a 2022 Ballotpedia candidate survey, Chaichi said housing is a human right (statement dates from her first campaign).
In a 2022 Ballotpedia candidate survey, Chaichi called for a single-payer, Medicare for All style system.
positions.excerpt: We need a single-payer – Medicare for All style – system where everyone is completely covered.

positions.statement: Chaichi cites helping secure funding to create affordable housing units in Beaverton.
positions.excerpt: I've helped secure funding to create affordable housing units in Beaverton.

positions.statement: Chaichi says she supports requiring large multinational corporations and the top 1% to pay their fair share to fund universal programs.
positions.excerpt: requiring large multinational corporations and the top 1% of wealthy individuals pay their fair share so we can ALL thrive

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 54

positions.statement: Chaichi cites spearheading legislation requiring law enforcement to unmask and identify themselves.
positions.excerpt: I spearheaded legislation in February requiring law enforcement to unmask and clearly identify themselves

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 54

positions.statement: Chaichi says she has helped secure funding for affordable housing in Beaverton.
positions.excerpt: Housing and Healthcare are Human Rights

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 54

positions.statement: Chaichi says she supports universal single-payer healthcare.
positions.excerpt: We must continue fighting to keep all Oregonians housed and healthy and for universal single payer healthcare.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet (Washington County edition), p. 54

voting_record.statement: OPB reported in January 2026 that Chaichi introduced the Law Enforcement Accountability and Visibility Act, concerning masks worn by law enforcement.
voting_record.excerpt: the Law Enforcement Accountability and Visibility Act, introduced by Rep. Farrah Chaichi, D-Beaverton

voting_record.statement: OPB reported in August 2026 that Chaichi led a lawmakers' letter to the Department of Corrections asking for no more than 15 consecutive days in solitary confinement.
voting_record.excerpt: a number of lawmakers, led by Rep. Farrah Chaichi, send a letter to the Dept. of Corrections

gaps: Did not respond to the Capital Chronicle 2026 questionnaire (all items 'No response')
Housing and healthcare positions are from a 2022 survey; no 2026 statement found
